_about: Lore data (docs/lore/README.md; decisions 257, 258): entries with facts, each fact saying who knows it. Code uses only status agreed. Facts, never lines to say.

entries.name: the Blood Rot's land
entries.summary: The region the Blood Rot raid, with their mine at its heart and the town at a distance from it.

facts.text: The land around the mine is dead: no crops, no beasts, nothing living.
Other regions lie beyond the Blood Rot's land.

entries.name: the Woodlands
entries.summary: The Woodlands, where Umbrage sits, with the farmsteads and fields around it, far from the mine (Jeff, 2026-10-22: "Held sit in the Woodlands"; the town renamed Umbrage, Jeff 2026-10-24).

facts.text: Umbrage sits in the Woodlands.
Farmsteads and fields lie near the town.

entries.name: the town
entries.summary: Where the players and their companions belong, and where the stockpile is.

entries.name: the old farmstead
entries.summary: An old farmstead in the wilds, abandoned, with tools and bandages left inside (Jeff, 2026-10-22); not the Blood Rot's doing.

facts.text: The old farmstead in the wilds stands abandoned; tools and bandages lie inside.

entries.name: the Old Tower
entries.summary: The Old Tower across the river from Umbrage: a broken-down castle the ancients lived in, conquered in the battle; its fallen warriors were buried before the people moved on, and nothing is known of them since. Snagfin keeps his counter there (Jeff, 2026-10-22).

facts.text: The Old Tower, across the river from Umbrage, is a broken-down castle the ancients lived in.
The Old Tower, the ancients' castle, was conquered in the battle, and its fallen warriors were buried before the people moved on.
Nothing is known of the ancients' history, or of them since they left.
No dead lie by the Old Tower: the dead are in the barrows, and the tower is where they lived.
Snagfin the goblin keeps his counter in the Old Tower.

entries.name: the temple
entries.summary: The town's temple, kept by a priest, where the fallen are brought back.

facts.text: The town has a temple, and a priest keeps it.

entries.name: the healer's hut
entries.summary: A healer's hut out in the wilds, where a medicine man lives and the fallen are brought back.

facts.text: Out in the wilds stands a healer's hut, where a medicine man lives.

entries.name: Cravenhold
entries.summary: The orc stronghold, outside the forest, in a land where the trees have been stripped (Jeff, 2026-10-27; maps' world_plane place "stronghold").

facts.text: Cravenhold is the orc stronghold, outside the forest, in a land where the trees have been stripped.

entries.name: the castle
entries.summary: An ancient, dilapidated castle built by dwarven stone smiths over a known entrance to the shifting labyrinths, to guard it; mostly overrun now (docs/lore/castle.md).

facts.text: The castle is ancient and dilapidated.
The castle was built by dwarven stone smiths, plain and utilitarian.
The dwarves built the castle over the labyrinths, as a cover over a known entrance, to guard it.
The castle guards a treasure that was rumoured and never found.
The castle is no longer dwarven; it is mostly overrun.
The maps of the labyrinths below the castle were lost long ago.
The labyrinths shift: their ways are never the same twice for long, which is why their treasures were never carried out and why adventurers still come.
Dwarven artifacts come from the dungeons below the castle.
Who has overrun the castle: the Blood Rot, their orc or kobold allies, something from below, or several at once.

entries.name: the mine
entries.summary: An old mine, the heart of the Blood Rot's land, over the fallen star.

facts.text: The old mine is the heart of the Blood Rot's land, and they live in and around it.
The deeper into the mine, the stronger the Blood Rot are.
The mine was dug toward where the star fell.

entries.name: the tower over the mine
entries.summary: A tower over the mine, built by orcs to dark elven designs, whose shifting inside still holds old artifacts and treasures.

facts.text: A tower stands over the mine.
The tower over the mine was built by orcish labour to the designs of dark elven architects, in their majestic style.
The tower over the mine holds old artifacts and treasures; dark elven artifacts come from it.
The inside of the tower over the mine shifts, perhaps by magic; its treasures have never all been carried out, and adventurers still come.

entries.name: the fallen star
entries.summary: Deep in the mine lies the source of the rot: a star that fell into the land many thousands of years ago.

facts.text: Deep in the Blood Rot's mine lies a fallen star, the source of the rot.
Common folk call it a fallen star.
Those who live near the mine call it the rot-source.
Those the Blood Rot take are carried down toward the star and are not seen again.
